subject: Art & Design
title: Brand Positioning: Owning a Space in the Mind
description: One-minute skill: Brand Positioning: Owning a Space in the Mind.

hook.text: When you think 'search engine,' you think Google. When you think 'tissue,' you say Kleenex. That's positioning.

buildup.text: Brand positioning is about occupying a unique, desirable spot in the customer's mind relative to competitors.

discovery.text: Positioning requires sacrifice: you can't be everything. Apple chose 'creative premium.' Dell chose 'affordable power.'

twist.text: You don't position against competitors directly — you position against alternatives.

climax.text: Brand Positioning matters because clearer reasoning leads to better judgments.

punchline.text: Positioning isn't what you do to the product.

quiz.question: What does effective brand positioning require?
options: Occupying a unique space in the customer's mind — which requires sacrifice

details.summary: Brand positioning defines how a brand occupies a unique space in the consumer's mind relative to competitors. Volvo owns 'safety,' FedEx owns 'overnight delivery,' and Apple owns 'creative innovation.' Effective positioning is narrow, differentiated, and defensible — you can't own everything.
details.whyItMatters: Without clear positioning, a brand is generic and interchangeable. Positioning answers the question 'why choose us?' in a single clear idea, giving customers a reason to prefer one brand over identical alternatives.
takeaways: Positioning defines a unique space in the consumer's mind
Volvo owns safety; FedEx owns overnight delivery
Effective positioning is narrow, differentiated, and defensible

faq.question: How does a brand find its positioning?
faq.answer: Research what competitors claim, what customers actually want but can't find, and what the brand genuinely does better than anyone else. The sweet spot is where a real brand strength meets an unmet customer need that no competitor has claimed. Test it with real customers.

faq.question: Can a brand change its positioning?
faq.answer: Yes, but it's difficult and risky. Repositioning requires changing every touchpoint — messaging, visual identity, product development, and customer experience. Old Spice successfully repositioned from an older men's brand to young and irreverent, but many repositioning attempts fail.
